linear_title: All runtime guides (Getting started / Manual setup)
body:
Docs changes for the Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare guides that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/node/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/node>), [`quickstarts/bun/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/bun>), [`quickstarts/deno/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/deno>), [`quickstarts/cloudflare/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/cloudflare>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

- [ ] **P0** · DOC-R1 · The stream-mode includes call static the default
  The three stream-mode includes present stream mode as opt-in, in four places. `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.bun.mdx:5`, `javascript.deno.mdx:5` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:8` (Cloudflare Pages) and `:35` (Cloudflare Workers) all say "Opt in by setting the `traceLifecycle` option to `'stream'`", and each file closes with "set `traceLifecycle` to `'static'` (the default)" (`javascript.bun.mdx:25`, `javascript.deno.mdx:24`, `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:62`).
  On develop the default is `'stream'`. `packages/core/src/client.ts:243` (`:242` at the pin) normalizes `traceLifecycle: options.traceLifecycle === 'static' ? 'static' : 'stream'`, and the comment directly above it (`:237-238`) states the same rule: every value except an explicit `'static'` resolves to stream. No runtime overrides it. Cloudflare reads `SENTRY_TRACE_LIFECYCLE` at `packages/cloudflare/src/options.ts:73`, but that read returns `undefined` when the variable is unset (`:107-109`), so it never changes the default, and `packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-serve.ts:28` describes `'stream'` as the default too.
  The docs already say this on another page: `docs/platforms/javascript/common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:23` calls stream mode "the new default", and `:198` tells the reader to set `traceLifecycle: 'static'`, or the `SENTRY_TRACE_LIFECYCLE=static` environment variable, to keep the previous model. The includes contradict the migration guide on the same site.
  **Change:** Reframe all four opt-in sentences as opt-out (`javascript.bun.mdx:5`, `javascript.deno.mdx:5`, `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:8` and `:35`): `'stream'` is the default, `'static'` is what a user sets. Replace the `traceLifecycle: "stream"` sample lines with `"static"` examples, or drop them. Add the missing comma after `tracesSampleRate: 0.2` in the Pages snippet at `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:19`; the Workers snippet at `:40-56` already parses. Match the wording of `migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:23` and `:198`, including the `SENTRY_TRACE_LIFECYCLE=static` escape hatch. Confirmed on Node on 2026-09-09: with no `traceLifecycle` option every Elysia span carried `sentry.trace_lifecycle: stream` and only span envelopes arrived; transaction envelopes needed an explicit `'static'` (QS-elysia, variants guide and static).
  Draft: [Fix inverted traceLifecycle default in the stream mode includes](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#28-fix-inverted-tracelifecycle-default-in-the-stream-mode-includes>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q1 · The verify step and the stream-mode includes describe the static lifecycle as the default
  The tracing verify step tells the reader to wrap work in `Sentry.startSpan({ op: "test", name: "My First Test Transaction" })`: `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.node.mdx:38-53`, `guides/bun/index.mdx:156-172`, `guides/deno/index.mdx:176-190` and `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:313-335`. The sentence that follows each one sends the reader to Sentry "to view the collected data" (`getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:120`, `bun/index.mdx:188`, `deno/index.mdx:207`, `cloudflare/index.mdx:364`) and expands the `quick-start-locate-data-expandable` include, which points at the Traces page. The only place the word "Transaction" appears is the sample name inside the snippet.
  Observed on `develop`, on all four runtimes with the documented wiring: no `transaction` envelope is sent at all. The manual span arrives as a child item inside a `span` envelope together with the server span, for example `["http.client GET 127.0.0.1", "test My First Test Span", "http.server GET"]`, because `packages/core/src/client.ts:243` normalizes any `traceLifecycle` other than `'static'` to `'stream'`. On the released line there is no such normalization, so `'static'` is the default and a transaction is sent: the pages are correct for the version they serve today and become wrong with v11.
  **Change:** On each of the four verify steps, describe what arrives: a trace with a server segment span and the manual span as its child, no transaction. Rename the sample from "My First Test Transaction" to a span name. Link the stream lifecycle page, and note that `traceLifecycle: "static"` restores the transaction envelope for readers who look for it. Fix the ten `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.*.mdx` files whose closing line calls `traceLifecycle` `'static'` "(the default)": node `:36`, cloudflare `:62`, hono `:51`, deno `:24`, and bun, nextjs, nestjs, nitro, gcp-functions and elysia at `:25`. Rewrite `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:382-388`, which frames the static lifecycle as the current model and stream as the opt-in. Apply the same rewrite to the framework verify includes: `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.express.mdx:30` and `:40` name "My First Test Transaction", and the Express run received the span as an `op: test` child of the `http.server` segment inside a span envelope, never a transaction envelope (QS-express, variants import and express5); `getting-started-verify/javascript.fastify.mdx:24-30` and `:40` and `guides/fastify/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` say the same and the Fastify run saw the same (QS-fastify, every variant); `getting-started-verify/javascript.koa.mdx:29` and `:35-46` and `guides/koa/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` likewise (QS-koa, every variant), as do `getting-started-verify/javascript.hapi.mdx:34` and `:47` and `guides/hapi/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` (QS-hapi, every variant), and `getting-started-verify/javascript.connect.mdx:30` and `:36-47`, `guides/connect/tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` and `includes/node-automatic-instrumentation.mdx:1-3` (QS-connect, every variant that starts), and `getting-started-verify/javascript.hono.mdx:30` plus the `getting-started-config/javascript.hono.mdx:21` and `:57` comment about 100% of transactions (QS-hono, every variant); the Hono guide page itself already says spans at `guides/hono/index.mdx:184`; the NestJS verify include is covered by DOC-Q57; the Google Cloud Functions config include says 100% of transactions at `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.gcp-functions.mdx:19` and its `tracing/instrumentation/automatic-instrumentation.mdx:3` explains transactions, while the invocation arrives as a `function.gcp` segment with the test span as its child (QS-gcp-functions, variant http-tracing). The Pages run confirmed the Cloudflare paragraph at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:382-384`: with no `traceLifecycle` option every trace arrived as span items and the `waitUntil` spans as later span envelopes, so stream is the default and static the opt-out (QS-cloudflare-pages, variant base).
  Draft: [Rewrite the tracing verify step for the stream lifecycle on the Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare guides](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#104-rewrite-the-tracing-verify-step-for-the-stream-lifecycle-on-the-node-bun-deno-and-cloudflare-guides>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q3 · Nothing on the four guides says where a route name comes from
  The four guides end their verify step without saying anything about how server spans are named: `getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:120`, `guides/bun/index.mdx:188`, `guides/deno/index.mdx:207`, `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:364` each send the reader to Sentry "to view the collected data" and expand an include that points at the Traces page. Nothing on the way there says where a route name comes from, so a reader who sees `GET` has no page to check.
  Observed on `develop` with the base setup: a plain `node:http` server on Node names every segment span `GET` and sets no `sentry.source`; `Deno.serve` names every span `GET` with source `url`, a `URLPattern` route included; `withSentry` on Workers names every span `GET` with source `url`; only `Bun.serve` with a `routes` map produces `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, and falls back to `GET` for an unrouted path. On Bun and Cloudflare the error event carries no `transaction` field, so an issue shows no route either; on Node the same event does carry `transaction: "GET /debug-sentry"`. Route names appear once a framework integration is in place, as the framework matrix records.
  **Change:** On each guide, state that the base setup names server spans by method (or URL under the static lifecycle) and that route names come from a framework integration, or on Bun from the `Bun.serve` routes map. Link the framework pages for the runtime from that sentence. On the Bun and Cloudflare guides, drop the claim that issues are grouped by transaction until the SDK sets the field. The Node guide can keep it: the Node error event does carry the transaction name.
  Draft: [State on the four guides that route names need a framework integration or a routes map](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#106-state-on-the-four-guides-that-route-names-need-a-framework-integration-or-a-routes-map>)

## Should land

- [ ] **P2** · X1 · "Tracing is enabled by default" on the first page of all three guides
  `platform-includes/performance/enable-tracing/javascript.bun.mdx:1`, `javascript.deno.mdx:1` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1` each read "Tracing is enabled by default in the Sentry <Runtime> SDK." The guides for those runtimes, and `platform-includes/performance/enable-automatic-instrumentation/javascript.bun.mdx:1` and `javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1`, tell the user to set `tracesSampleRate` or `tracesSampler`.
  What was observed: `hasSpansEnabled` in `packages/core/src/utils/hasSpansEnabled.ts:23-36` records spans only when `tracesSampleRate` or `tracesSampler` is set, on every runtime. On Bun there is a second gate on top of it: `getPerformanceIntegrations` in `packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:38-44` returns no performance integrations while `hasSpansEnabled` is false. The Deno and Cloudflare SDKs have no such gate and always install the tracing integrations, so the general reason the sentence is wrong is the sampling option, not the integration set.
  **Change:** Replace the first sentence in all three includes with a statement that tracing is enabled by setting `tracesSampleRate` or `tracesSampler` in `Sentry.init`, and that no spans are recorded when neither is set. Keep the wording consistent with the `enable-automatic-instrumentation` includes for Bun and Cloudflare, which already require the option. There is no Deno variant of that include, so Deno falls back to `javascript.mdx`.
  Draft: [Fix "Tracing is enabled by default" in the Bun, Deno and Cloudflare enable-tracing includes](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#155-fix-tracing-is-enabled-by-default-in-the-bun-deno-and-cloudflare-enable-tracing-includes>)

title: Node
body:
Docs changes for the Node guide that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/node/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/node>), [`quickstarts/express/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/express>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q85 · The Node install pages do not reflect the v11 install-method decision: --import main, bundler plus top-level import, @sentry/node/import with late init, no CommonJS option
  The SDK team settled the v11 install methods for Node on 2026-09-09 while aligning the in-product onboarding (Linear SDK-1446); the docs pages do not reflect the decision yet, and the getting-started runs show why it matters:
  - `node --import ./instrument.mjs` stays the main documented path, because it guarantees the runtime wrapping and instruments as early as possible. Every Node quick start delivered the full telemetry on that path.
  - An alternative page documents the bundler plugin plus a top-level import, and explains the difference: a plain first-line import is not enough on its own because ESM hoists the framework imports ahead of `Sentry.init`. The runs measured that nuance: Express, Fastify, Hapi and Hono still got their spans and errors from a first-line import (their instrumentation registers at runtime), Koa lost every router and middleware span and, without the deprecated handler, its error capture (DOC-Q28, DOC-Q45). The pattern `import "./instrument.mjs"; await import("./app.mjs");` makes a top-level import safe without a bundler.
  - An alternative page documents `--import @sentry/node/import` with a later `Sentry.init()`, replacing the late-initialization page that still rests on the removed `@sentry/node/preload` entry (DOC-Q26).
  - The CommonJS install option is dropped; the pages assume ESM.
  - Meta-frameworks are documented without `--import`, with an alternative that uses it and says when (for example when some packages are not bundled). Nuxt no longer emits the server config into the build, so it cannot be `--import`ed at all (DOC-F11).

  **Change:** Rework `common/install/index.mdx`, `esm.mdx`, `esm-without-import.mdx`, `commonjs.mdx` and `late-initialization.mdx` to the three methods above, record the decision on the pages rather than in a chat thread, and align the in-product onboarding snippets with it.
  Draft: [Restructure the Node install methods for v11: --import as the main path, bundler plus top-level import and --import @sentry/node/import as the alternatives, no CommonJS option](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#107-restructure-the-node-install-methods-for-v11---import-as-the-main-path-bundler-plus-top-level-import-and---import-sentrynodeimport-as-the-alternatives-no-commonjs-option>)
- [ ] **P0** · DOC-Q25 · The Express, Fastify, Koa, Hapi and Connect ESM tabs import the instrument file without its extension
  `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.express.mdx:22` starts the ESM app with `import "./instrument";`, while the config step creates `instrument.mjs`. Node ESM does not probe extensions: the app never starts, `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find module .../instrument ... Did you mean to import "./instrument.js"?`. With `import "./instrument.mjs"` the same app produces exactly the `--import` output. The same extensionless import sits at `common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:55`, and the orphaned `platform-includes/getting-started-add-top-level-import/javascript.express.mdx` imports `./instrument.js`. The Fastify tab has the same defect at `platform-includes/getting-started-use/javascript.fastify.mdx:20`, with the same `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` (QS-fastify, variant esm-tab), and so does the Koa tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.koa.mdx:20`; on Koa the corrected first-line import starts the app but loses every router and middleware span and the route names, so the Koa tab should rely on the `node --import` command instead (QS-koa, variants esm-tab and self-import). The Hapi tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.hapi.mdx:28` fails the same way, and its corrected first-line import loses nothing (QS-hapi, variants esm-tab and self-import), and so does the Connect tab at `getting-started-use/javascript.connect.mdx:20` (QS-connect, variant esm-tab). The NestJS guide has its own page, `guides/nestjs/install/esm-without-import.mdx:41-51`, whose `main.ts` imports `./instrument` without extension and does not start as ESM either (QS-nestjs, variant esm-verbatim).
  **Change:** Import `./instrument.mjs` in the Express, Fastify, Hapi and Connect ESM tabs, drop the import from the Koa tab in favour of `--import`, matching the file the config step creates, and fix `esm-without-import.mdx:55` the same way.
  Draft: [Fix the extensionless instrument import on the Express, Fastify, Koa, Hapi and Connect guides and the esm-without-import page](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#5-fix-the-extensionless-instrument-import-on-the-express-fastify-koa-hapi-and-connect-guides-and-the-esm-without-import-page>)
- [ ] **P0** · DOC-Q26 · The late-initialization page rests on the removed @sentry/node/preload entry
  `common/install/late-initialization.mdx` (supported by the Node, Connect, Express, Fastify, Hapi, Hono and Koa guides) tells readers to run `node --require @sentry/node/preload app.js` (`:37`) or `node --import @sentry/node/preload app.js` (`:68`) and to select modules with `SENTRY_PRELOAD_INTEGRATIONS` (`:106`, `:132`).
  Observed on develop: `Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './preload' is not defined by "exports" in @sentry/node/package.json`; the package exports `.`, `./import`, `./vite`, `./rollup`, `./webpack` and `./esbuild` only. `common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1359` records that the `init`, `preload` and `loader` entry points were removed from every server SDK, and names the replacement: `--import` the SDK and call `Sentry.init()` later. The Fastify run hit the same error; the page lists Fastify at `:9` and `:114` (QS-fastify, variant late-init), as did the Koa run, with Koa listed at `:116` (QS-koa, variant late-init), and the Hapi run, with Hapi listed at `:115` (QS-hapi, variant late-init), and the Connect run, with Connect listed at `:113` although no Connect integration exists to preload (QS-connect, variant late-init), and the Hono run, with Hono listed at `:11` (QS-hono, variant late-init).
  **Change:** Rewrite the page around `node --import @sentry/node/import app.mjs` with a later `Sentry.init()`, the replacement the SDK team settled on 2026-09-09 (DOC-Q85), and drop `@sentry/node/preload` and `SENTRY_PRELOAD_INTEGRATIONS`.
  Draft: [Rewrite or remove the late-initialization install page for v11](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#6-rewrite-or-remove-the-late-initialization-install-page-for-v11>)

## Should land

- [ ] **P2** · DOC-Q5 · --require banner, and a first-line ESM import equals --import
  `platform-includes/getting-started-node/javascript.mdx:93-96` shows `node --import ./instrument.mjs app.mjs`, and `:55` warns that importing the instrument file later than first means auto-instrumentation and modules like database monitoring may not work. Nothing on the page mentions `--require`.
  Observed on `develop` with Node v26.5.0: `node --require ./instrument.cjs app.mjs` still delivers the same errors, spans, headers and logs, but its first stderr line is `[Sentry] Initializing the SDK via the Node --require flag is no longer supported, because Node re-runs --require preloads on its module loader thread. Use --import instead`, printed from `packages/node/src/sdk/index.ts:126-133` whenever `getEntryPointType() === 'require'`, unconditionally and not behind `debug`. A first-line `import "./instrument.mjs"` in the entry file gives the same telemetry as the flag, including Express route names and handler spans, because the injection hook is registered while `@sentry/node` evaluates. `NODE_OPTIONS="--import ./instrument.mjs"` is identical to the flag.
  **Change:** Add one sentence that `--require` is no longer supported for initializing the SDK and prints a banner, with the `--import` replacement. Keep it narrow: `common/install/late-initialization.mdx:34,37,106,132` recommends `node --require @sentry/node/preload app.js`, which no longer resolves on develop, because the `preload` entry point was removed from every server SDK (see DOC-Q26); the warning against `--require` can therefore stand without that exception. Soften the ordering warning at `:55`: a first-line ESM import of the instrument file is equivalent to `--import`; the warning applies to imports that are not first. Surface `NODE_OPTIONS` as an equivalent form on this page; it is already documented at `common/install/esm.mdx:44-48`.
  Draft: [Update the Node getting-started page for --require and for first-line ESM imports](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#163-update-the-node-getting-started-page-for---require-and-for-first-line-esm-imports>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q28 · The esm-without-import page says a first-line import cannot instrument frameworks; Express, Fastify, Hapi and Hono are
  `common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:28-30` says that with a direct first-line import only native Node.js APIs can be instrumented and the SDK will not capture framework-specific data. Observed on develop: `import "./instrument.mjs"` as the first line of the Express app produced exactly the `--import` output, with middleware and handler spans, route-named segments (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`) and `auto.http.express` error events; the Node run's Express check saw the same, and the Fastify run got the same hook and handler spans and `auto.function.fastify` events from a first-line import (QS-fastify, variant self-import). Koa is the counter-example: its first-line import produced url-named `GET` segments and no router or middleware span (QS-koa, variant self-import), so the page should name what is covered and what is not instead of a blanket warning. Hapi behaves like Fastify: the first-line import produced the same items as `--import`, every Hapi span, route name and error (QS-hapi, variant self-import). Hono too: `sentry(app)` patches the app instance at registration time, and the first-line import produced the same route-named segments, middleware spans and errors as `--import` (QS-hono, variant self-import).
  **Change:** Turn the page into the bundler-plus-top-level-import method the SDK team settled on 2026-09-09 (DOC-Q85): say that a plain first-line import instruments only what registers at runtime (measured: Express, Fastify, Hapi and Hono yes, Koa no), show `import "./instrument.mjs"; await import("./app.mjs");` as the bundler-free way to keep the init ahead of the framework, and name the bundler plugin as the way to instrument everything without `--import`; the NestJS copy of the page, `guides/nestjs/install/esm-without-import.mdx:18-20`, needs the same qualification, since the guide's default CommonJS build gets full Nest and Express spans from a first-line import (QS-nestjs, variant cjs).
  Draft: [Correct the first-line import limitation on the esm-without-import page for v11](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#115-correct-the-first-line-import-limitation-on-the-esm-without-import-page-for-v11>)

title: Express
body:
Docs changes for the Express guide that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/express/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/express>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

None.

## Should land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q27 · The Express and Connect async verify snippets hang on Express 4 and Connect 3
  `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.express.mdx:36-47` replaces the `/debug-sentry` route with an `async` handler that throws inside `Sentry.startSpan`. On express 4.22.2 the request never gets a response (the client timed out, status 000) and the error arrives as `auto.node.onunhandledrejection`, not through the Express error path; the request segment reports status `ok` with `http.response.status_code: 200` although nothing was sent. On express 5.2.1 the same snippet answers 500 and the error is captured as `auto.http.express`. The guide names no Express major; the registry's `express` is 5. The Connect include `getting-started-verify/javascript.connect.mdx:36-47` has the same shape and the same result on connect 3.7.0: no response, the error as `auto.node.onunhandledrejection`, and the segment closed with status `ok` when the client gave up (QS-connect, variant no-handler).
  **Change:** Say that the async snippet needs Express 5, or add a `try/catch` that calls `next(err)` so it works on Express 4 and on Connect as well.
  Draft: [Make the async tracing verify snippets work on Express 4 and Connect 3, or state what they need](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#114-make-the-async-tracing-verify-snippets-work-on-express-4-and-connect-3-or-state-what-they-need>)

title: Fastify
body:
Docs changes for the Fastify guide that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/fastify/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/fastify>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

- [ ] **P0** · DOC-Q37 · The Fastify error handler page imports from a package that does not exist
  `guides/fastify/features/error-handler.mdx:14` reads `import { setupFastifyErrorHandler } from "@sentry/fastify";`. No such package exists, in the develop tarballs or in the monorepo's `packages/`: the snippet fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package '@sentry/fastify'`. It also calls `fastify()` at `:16` without importing it.

  `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.hono.mdx:36-47` tells the reader to call `Sentry.startSpan` in the `/debug-sentry` route. No Hono snippet imports `Sentry` into the app file: `guides/hono/index.mdx:264-267` imports only `{ sentry }`, and `:71` says `@sentry/node` is not imported directly. Pasted verbatim the route throws `ReferenceError: Sentry is not defined`, captured as the error, with no test span. `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/hono"` does not help: the package root exports nothing, and the route throws `TypeError: Sentry.startSpan is not a function`.   `guides/hono/index.mdx:168` says to import from `@sentry/hono/node`, not `@sentry/node`. The install pages render the opposite: `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.hono.mdx:2` and `:38` (through `common/install/commonjs.mdx:25`), `common/install/esm.mdx:25` and `common/install/esm-without-import.mdx:39` initialize from `@sentry/node`. With `@sentry/hono/node` the warning disappears and the SDK name is right.

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-F1 · Hono on Bun
  The Hono guide names Bun at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12`, has a Bun install tab at `hono/index.mdx:84-86` and a Bun setup snippet at `hono/index.mdx:278-300`, but it never shows how to start the app or what the runtime delivers. The Bun guide teaches only `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js` (`bun/index.mdx:100`) and carries a "Bundled Code Limitation" alert at `bun/index.mdx:90-94`. `sentryBunPlugin`, `@sentry/bun/plugin` and `Bun.build` appear nowhere in the docs.
  Verified on Hono 4.13.x with `@sentry/hono/bun` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0 and re-run on 1.4.2: install `@sentry/hono` plus `@sentry/bun`, call `app.use(sentry(app, { dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }))` on a fresh `new Hono()`, export `{ port, fetch: app.fetch }`, and run `bun app.ts`. No instrument file and no `--preload` are needed, because the middleware calls `Sentry.init` itself. `traceLifecycle` defaults to `stream` on this line, which names the request span `http.server GET /users/:id` and the database span `db SELECT users`; under `traceLifecycle: 'static'` the same run gives a transaction `GET /users/:id` and a span `db SELECT * FROM users`. One Bun bug needs a workaround: Bun garbage-collects a `node:diagnostics_channel` channel that only Sentry's subscriber holds, so a driver whose first query happens later in the process silently loses its spans; pin the channels by keeping a strong reference right after the middleware is registered, `globalThis.__sentryPinnedChannels ??= ['mysql2:query', 'mysql2:execute', 'mysql2:connect', 'mysql2:pool:connect'].map(name => dc.tracingChannel(name))`, which is harmless on Node. Building the same entry with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and running `bun dist/app.js` adds spans for `mysql`@2; the bundled captures cover errors, route names, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch`, both database drivers and logs, and do not drive the isolation route.
  Works today:
  - Unhandled handler errors, with the route as the transaction name
  - Parameterized route names (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`)
  - Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
  - Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation
  - Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
  - `mysql2` 3.20.0+ database spans with no build step, as long as the driver is loaded and queried early or the channels are pinned as above
  - `Sentry.logger` log envelopes, flushed on a roughly 5 second timer and needing no `enableLogs` option
  Known limits:
  - Drivers that do not publish `node:diagnostics_channel` events themselves, such as `mysql`@2, produce spans only in the `Bun.build` bundle.
  - Do not pass `external: ["@sentry/*"]` to `Bun.build` for a Hono app. Externalizing `@sentry/*` while `hono` is inlined gives two copies of hono's `GET_MATCH_RESULT` symbol and every request 500s inside `@sentry/hono`'s `requestHandler`. Either pass no `external` at all (the verified recipe), or externalize `hono` together with `@sentry/*`, which then behaves exactly like the unbundled run.

  **Change:** `guides/hono/index.mdx`: add a "Run your app" step with a Bun tab showing `bun app.ts` and the `Bun.build` + `sentryBunPlugin()` variant, state that the `--preload` step is not needed here, and name the span names a reader will see under the `stream` default and under `static`. `guides/bun/index.mdx:90-94`: rewrite the alert so it describes the plugin build as the supported way to instrument bundled code. `packages/hono/README.md:172-190`: the Bun section ends in the Node recipe (`serve` from `@hono/node-server`); replace it with the `export default app` form the docs page shows.
  Draft: [Document Hono on Bun: unbundled run and the Bun.build plugin variant](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#53-document-hono-on-bun-unbundled-run-and-the-bunbuild-plugin-variant>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-F18 · Hono on Deno
  The Hono guide already claims Deno support: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12` lists Deno among the runtimes, `:88-89` gives the Deno peer dependency as `deno add npm:@sentry/deno`, and `:302-324` shows the Deno tab with `import { sentry } from "@sentry/hono/deno"`, `app.use(sentry(app, {...}))` and `Deno.serve(app.fetch)`. The page carries no runtime caveats around `:360`, and `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/deno/index.mdx:1-230` never mentions `node_modules`, `nodeModulesDir`, the `@sentry/deno/import` hook or outgoing `fetch`.
  Verified on Hono 4.13.7 with `@sentry/hono/deno` 10.67.0 on Deno 2.9.0: install `@sentry/hono` and `@sentry/deno` into a real on-disk `node_modules` with `npm install`, set `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` in `deno.json`, put `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line of the entry file when you want database and library spans, then wire the middleware exactly as the current snippet shows and run `deno run --allow-net --allow-env --allow-read --allow-sys main.ts`.
  Works today:
  - Unhandled route errors, with `transaction: "GET /error"` and mechanism `auto.http.hono.context_error`. Hono turns the throw into its own 500 response and the middleware's `responseHandler` reads `context.error`, so the event still arrives and the server span is marked `internal_error`.
  - Parameterized names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`.
  - Per-request isolation across concurrent requests.
  - Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation.
  - Database spans for `mysql` (requires the import hook line).
  - Logs.
  Known limits:
  - Outgoing `fetch()` is not instrumented on Deno: no `http.client` span and no `sentry-trace`/`baggage` headers, so the downstream service starts a new trace. The default integrations of `@sentry/deno` carry `denoHttpIntegration()` for `node:http`/`node:https` and nothing that traces `fetch`; the breadcrumb integration patches `fetch`, so the call is still breadcrumbed while no span is started and no header is injected.
  - `node:http`/`node:https` clients are traced normally.
  - Without the import hook line, database and library spans are silently missing.

  **Change:** `guides/hono/index.mdx:88-89`: show the `deno.json` and the npm-based install, not `deno add` alone. `guides/hono/index.mdx` near `:302-324`: note the optional `@sentry/deno/import` first line and the permission flags. `guides/hono/index.mdx` near `:360`: add a Deno-only caveat for outgoing `fetch`, naming `node:http`/`node:https` as the clients that are traced. `guides/deno/index.mdx`: add an "Outgoing fetch requests" section stating the same limit.
  Draft: [Document the verified Hono on Deno setup and its outgoing fetch limit](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#68-document-the-verified-hono-on-deno-setup-and-its-outgoing-fetch-limit>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-F35 · Hono on Workers
  The Hono guide already treats Cloudflare Workers as a first-class tab: `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx:12` names Cloudflare Workers as a supported runtime, `:65-78` tells Workers users to install `@sentry/cloudflare` as a peer dependency they never import, `:129-144` is the "Cloudflare Workers: Enable Node.js Compatibility" Expandable, and `:240-262` (the Cloudflare Workers tab of "Add the Sentry Middleware") shows the `sentry(app, {...})` wiring. Two gaps: the Expandable sets `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]` but never `compatibility_date`, and the guide's only database sentence, `:162`, is Node.js-only.
  Verified on the develop line: `npm install @sentry/hono @sentry/cloudflare hono`, a `wrangler.jsonc` with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`, `app.use(sentry(app, { dsn, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }))` as the first middleware, `export default app`, run with `npx wrangler dev`. For database spans the same app is built through Vite instead, which needs three more packages, `npm install vite @cloudflare/vite-plugin mysql@2`, and a `vite.config.ts` with `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin({ autoInstrumentation: false })]` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`, with `autoInstrumentation: false` because the Hono middleware already applies `withSentry`.
  Works today:
  - Unhandled route errors, parameterized route names (`GET /users/:id`, source `route`), per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers, `Sentry.logger` logs.
  - `db` spans from a `mysql` query, through the Vite build only.
  Known limits:
  - A Worker bundled by `wrangler dev`/`wrangler deploy` alone emits no database spans and logs no warning.
  - No `middleware.hono` spans on Workers: the transaction's `spans[]` holds only the `db` and `http.client` children.

  **Change:** On `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/hono/index.mdx`: Extend the Expandable at `:129-144` to set `compatibility_date` alongside `nodejs_compat`, matching `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5`. Add a "Database spans on Cloudflare Workers" subsection after the "Add the Sentry Middleware" section (`:227-359`), before "### Report Unhandled Exceptions" at `:360`, stating that database instrumentation on Workers is build-time only, showing the Vite config above, and linking to `/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/features/vite-plugin/`. Say in the same subsection that a Workers transaction carries no `middleware.hono` spans, so readers do not go looking for them. Link that subsection from `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/hono.mdx`, the 8-line stub that today only redirects to the Hono guide, so a reader who starts on the Cloudflare side reaches the database note too.

Docs changes for the NestJS guide that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/nestjs/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/nestjs>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

- [ ] **P0** · DOC-Q57 · The NestJS tracing verify snippet kills the process
  `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.nestjs.mdx:30-49` updates `/debug-sentry` with `Sentry.startSpan(...)` whose callback throws inside `setTimeout(..., 99)`. The route answers 200 and the test span is sent, then the throw fires outside the Nest pipeline: captured as `auto.node.onuncaughtexception`, and the Nest process exits, so the app is dead after one hit. The snippet also shows no controller class and no `Sentry` import.
  **Change:** Throw synchronously inside the callback or await a delay, wrap the snippet in a controller with `import * as Sentry from "@sentry/nestjs"`, and say the result is a span inside the request trace.
  Draft: [Fix the NestJS tracing verify snippet: its delayed throw is an uncaught exception that exits the app](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#13-fix-the-nestjs-tracing-verify-snippet-its-delayed-throw-is-an-uncaught-exception-that-exits-the-app>)
- [ ] **P0** · DOC-Q58 · The NestJS ESM start script is not a runnable command
  `guides/nestjs/install/esm.mdx:33-36` shows `"start": "--import ./instrument.mjs nest start"`. Executed as an npm script it fails with `sh: --: invalid option`: the line names no `node` binary, and `nest start` does not accept `--import`. The `NODE_OPTIONS` form at `:41` works, as does `node --import ./dist/instrument.js dist/main.js`.
  **Change:** Show a real command such as `node --import ./instrument.mjs dist/main.js`, or lead with the `NODE_OPTIONS` form.
  Draft: [Replace the NestJS ESM start script with a command that runs](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#14-replace-the-nestjs-esm-start-script-with-a-command-that-runs>)

## Should land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q59 · No NestJS error reaches Sentry without SentryGlobalFilter; the guide says otherwise
  `platform-includes/getting-started-capture-errors/javascript.nestjs.mdx:1` says Sentry captures by default the unhandled exceptions that no error filter catches. With the guide's setup up to `guides/nestjs/index.mdx:102-117` (`SentryModule.forRoot()`, no filter) the unhandled controller error produced no event: Nest's built-in exception handler catches everything, and nothing reaches Sentry until `SentryGlobalFilter` or `@SentryExceptionCaptured()` is added. `:2` says HttpExceptions are not captured by default; that holds for 404, 503 and a bare `HttpException` with status 500 alike, the filter has no status threshold and no option, and `shouldHandleError` exists only for Express and Fastify.
  **Change:** State that Nest's default exception handler swallows every error, so the filter or the decorator is required for any HTTP error, move that step before Verify, and say that 5xx HttpExceptions are included with no option to change it.
  Draft: [Say on the NestJS guide that SentryGlobalFilter is required for any HTTP error to be captured, and move it before Verify](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#128-say-on-the-nestjs-guide-that-sentryglobalfilter-is-required-for-any-http-error-to-be-captured-and-move-it-before-verify>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q60 · The Nest integration page names the wrong mechanism, enablement rule and Nest 4
  `common/configuration/integrations/nest.mdx:19-21` says the integration is enabled with performance monitoring and captures spans using `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-nestjs-core`. That package is not installed (only `@opentelemetry/api` is); the Nest integration is installed with and without tracing (24 of 24 integrations in the errors-only run), and every Nest span comes from the SDK's own diagnostics-channel instrumentation (`auto.http.nestjs`, `auto.middleware.nestjs`). `:31` says Nest.js 4.0.0 or later is supported; the build injects into `@nestjs/core` 8 through 12 and the package peer range starts at 8.
  **Change:** Describe the built-in instrumentation of `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/schedule`, `@nestjs/event-emitter` and `@nestjs/bullmq`, say it is always installed, and list Nest.js 8 through 12.
  Draft: [Rewrite the Nest integration page around the diagnostics-channel instrumentation](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#129-rewrite-the-nest-integration-page-around-the-diagnostics-channel-instrumentation>)

title: Elysia
body:
Docs changes for the Elysia guide that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/elysia/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/elysia>), [`cells/M-elysia-cf/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/cells/M-elysia-cf>), [`cells/M-elysia-deno/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/cells/M-elysia-deno>), [`cells/M-elysia-bun/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/cells/M-elysia-bun>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

- [ ] **P0** · DOC-F36 · Elysia on Workers: runtime list says Bun or Node only
  No page mentions Elysia on Cloudflare Workers. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` lists the prerequisites as "Bun or Node.js 18+ (with @elysiajs/node adapter)" and the install tabs at `:55-60` plus the config snippet at `:82` cover Bun and Node only. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:3-5` promises a span for every Elysia lifecycle phase (`request_handler.elysia` for Handle, `middleware.elysia` for the rest) with no runtime qualifier, and `:9-12` has a "Runtime Behavior" section covering exactly two runtimes. The Cloudflare framework list at `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23` has no Elysia entry and `guides/cloudflare/frameworks/` has no `elysia.mdx`.
  Verified on the develop line: Elysia 1.4.30 on workerd with `compatibility_date: "2026-05-01"` and `compatibility_flags: ["nodejs_compat"]`. Install `@sentry/cloudflare @sentry/elysia elysia`. Construct the app as `withElysia(new Elysia({ aot: false }))` before any route is registered, and export `Sentry.withSentry((env) => ({ dsn: env.SENTRY_DSN, tracesSampleRate: 1.0 }), { fetch: request => app.fetch(request) })`. Do not call `init` from `@sentry/elysia` on Workers: its `sdk.js` imports `node:os` and `@sentry/bun`, so the Worker fails to build; `Sentry.withSentry` from `@sentry/cloudflare` is what supplies the client, and `withElysia` is the only part of `@sentry/elysia` used. Ahead-of-time compilation must be off: with the default, workerd refuses to start the Worker because Elysia's generated handler runs `new Function` and touches randomness in global scope. For database spans, build with Vite: `plugins: [cloudflare(), sentryCloudflareVitePlugin()]` from `@sentry/cloudflare/vite`, then `vite build` and point wrangler at the emitted config.
  Works today:
  - Unhandled errors via Elysia's global error hook, parameterized route names, per-request isolation, incoming trace continuation, outgoing `fetch` spans with headers, `Sentry.logger` logs, and `db` spans through the Vite build.
  Known limits:
  - A `wrangler`-bundled Worker emits no database spans.
  - No Elysia lifecycle spans on Workers: every transaction comes back with `spans: []`, because the `app.trace()` handler that creates them depends on `rootSpanForRequest`, which only the Bun branch of `app.wrap` populates.
  - `withElysia` must wrap the instance before routes are registered, or only the error path gets the route name.
  - `mysql2` on workerd needs `disableEval: true` in the connection options, and the pool must be created at module scope.

  **Change:** Add `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/cloudflare/frameworks/elysia.mdx` with the wiring above and list it at `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:16-23`. Add a Cloudflare Workers entry to `guides/elysia/index.mdx:25`, add a Cloudflare bullet to the Runtime Behavior list at `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12`, and scope the lifecycle-span promise at `:3-5` to Bun and Node so it no longer reads as universal.
  Draft: [Add an Elysia on Cloudflare Workers page and drop the Bun/Node-only runtime claim](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#33-add-an-elysia-on-cloudflare-workers-page-and-drop-the-bunnode-only-runtime-claim>)
- [ ] **P0** · DOC-F19 · Elysia on Deno: the documented init loses isolation and route names
  `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` lists prerequisites as Bun or Node 18+ with the node adapter, and the install and configure snippets at `:52-70` and `:78-120` have only Bun and Node tabs, with `Sentry.init` imported from `@sentry/elysia`. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:9-12` enumerates exactly two runtimes and `:6` claims parameterized route names unconditionally. A grep for `deno` over the Elysia guide returns nothing.
  Verified on Elysia 1.4.30 and Deno 2.9.0: install the packages with npm into a real `node_modules`, set `{"nodeModulesDir": "manual"}` in `deno.json`, and pick one of two wirings. (1) Call `Sentry.init()` from `@sentry/deno` before `Deno.serve` and import only `withElysia` (and `fetchIntegration`) from `@sentry/elysia`. (2) Keep `Sentry.init()` from `@sentry/elysia` and pass `integrations: [denoServeIntegration()]`, imported from `@sentry/deno`. Both need `@sentry/deno` installed alongside `@sentry/elysia`; both were exercised in the `static` and `stream` trace lifecycles. Mount with `Deno.serve({ port }, withElysia(new Elysia()).get(...).fetch)`. Add `import "@sentry/deno/import";` as the first line for database spans, and pass `integrations: [fetchIntegration()]` for outgoing requests.
  Works today:
  - Route errors, mechanism `auto.http.elysia.on_error`.
  - `GET /users/:id` with op `http.server` and source `route`, with the Elysia lifecycle phases as child spans.
  - Per-request isolation and incoming trace continuation, with either wiring.
  - Outgoing `http.client` spans plus `sentry-trace`/`baggage`, with `fetchIntegration()`, which `@sentry/elysia` exports (it re-exports the `@sentry/bun` integration).
  - Database spans for `mysql`, and logs.
  Known limits:
  - `@sentry/elysia`'s own `init()` on its own delegates to `@sentry/bun` and does not instrument `Deno.serve`: there is no `http.server` span, every Elysia lifecycle phase becomes its own root transaction on one process-wide trace, incoming trace headers are ignored and the isolation scope carries the previous request's route into the next event. An outgoing `fetch` still produces an `http.client` span under the default `stream` lifecycle, but as a parentless segment; under `static` it is dropped for having no active span.
  - The wiring decides the reported SDK: with `Sentry.init` from `@sentry/deno` events carry `sdk.name: sentry.javascript.deno`; with the `denoServeIntegration()` variant they keep `sentry.javascript.bun` and `contexts.runtime.name: bun`, and sessions are emitted.
  - `mysql2` cannot be imported while the Deno import hook is active: Deno compiles `require('*.json')` as JavaScript (denoland/deno#36240) and the import throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected token ':'`. Use `mysql@2`.

  **Change:** `guides/elysia/index.mdx:25` and the snippets at `:52-70`, `:78-120`: add Deno tabs with both wirings described above. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:6,9-12`: add a Deno bullet and qualify the route-name claim. `common/configuration/integrations/fetchIntegration.mdx:10`: it states the integration "only works inside the Cloudflare Workers runtime", which the Deno runs disprove.
  Draft: [Document Elysia on Deno: init from @sentry/deno, or add denoServeIntegration](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#34-document-elysia-on-deno-init-from-sentrydeno-or-add-denoserveintegration>)

## Should land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q64 · The verify route is added after listen() and is never served
  `guides/elysia/index.mdx:177-184` says to add the `/debug-sentry` route to the app, after a config snippet (`:124-126`) that ends in `.listen(3000)`. Under `@elysiajs/node` a route added after `.listen()` answers 404: `My first Sentry error!` is never thrown, and the only event is `Error: NOT_FOUND`, which looks like success. Chained before `.listen()` the route creates the issue (`auto.http.elysia.on_error`, transaction `GET /debug-sentry`, request data).
  **Change:** Show the verify route chained before `.listen()`, or say that routes must be defined before `listen`, and drop the "add the following route" framing.
  Draft: [Chain the Elysia verify route before .listen() on the guide](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#131-chain-the-elysia-verify-route-before-listen-on-the-guide>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q65 · Unmatched routes and status() throws are captured by default, the guide says otherwise
  `guides/elysia/index.mdx:139` says client errors (3xx and 4xx) are not captured by default. The default filter reads `context.set.status`, which is 200 for Elysia's `NotFoundError` (an unmatched route, 404 to the client) and 500 for anything thrown through `status(4xx, ...)`: both are captured, `Error: NOT_FOUND` once per process because Elysia reuses one instance, and a `status()` throw as `'ElysiaCustomStatusResponse' captured as exception with keys: code, response`. Only `set.status = 4xx` before a throw is skipped. The guide's own `shouldHandleError` snippet (`:146-151`) suppresses them.
  **Change:** State that unmatched routes and `status()`-thrown responses are captured by default, that `status()` throws arrive as non-Error objects, and point at `shouldHandleError` as the filter.
  Draft: [Correct the default error filter description on the Elysia guide](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#132-correct-the-default-error-filter-description-on-the-elysia-guide>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-F2 · Elysia on Bun
  The Bun wiring on the Elysia guide is correct; three statements around it are not. `docs/platforms/javascript/guides/elysia/index.mdx:4-5` declares `sdk: sentry.javascript.elysia` with `fallbackGuide: javascript.bun`, `elysia/index.mdx:23-25` lists the prerequisites, `elysia/index.mdx:56` shows `bun add @sentry/elysia`, and the alert at `elysia/index.mdx:47-50` ("You do **not** need `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`") is confirmed by the run. The defects are in the includes: `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:1` opens this server guide with a `BrowserTracing` paragraph; `javascript.elysia.mdx:5` claims the ops are `request_handler.elysia` and `middleware.elysia` where the observed ops are plain `handler` and `middleware`; and `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.elysia.mdx:25` says `'static'` is "the default" where this line defaults to `'stream'`. On top of that, nothing on the page or in its includes says how database and library instrumentation behaves on Bun.
  Verified on Elysia 1.4 with `@sentry/elysia` 10.67.0 (develop, 6f2da7483d) on Bun 1.4.0: `Sentry.init` either inline in the entry or in an `instrument.ts` imported first, `Sentry.withElysia(new Elysia())` wrapping the fresh instance before any route is chained, then `bun app.ts`. No `--preload`, no `@elysiajs/opentelemetry`, and no build step for the base capabilities. For libraries that need the plugin build, build with `Bun.build({ entrypoints: ['./app.ts'], outdir: './dist', target: 'bun', sourcemap: 'external', plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` and run `bun dist/app.js`. Pass no `external` at all, and no `packages: 'external'` or `packages: '*'`: the follow-up run recorded that any of those puts the instrumented packages back outside the bundle and the spans disappear again. `sentryBunPlugin()` is build-only; calling `Bun.plugin(sentryBunPlugin())` from a `--preload` file crashes the app at import.
  Works today:
  - Unhandled handler errors via the SDK's global `onError` hook
  - Route names `GET /users/:id` with source `route`, on the success and error paths
  - Per-request isolation across concurrent requests
  - Incoming `sentry-trace`/`baggage` continuation, plus response trace headers
  - Outgoing `fetch` spans with propagation headers
  - `mysql2` database spans under a plain `bun app.ts`; database instrumentation as a whole is recorded partial, and this is the half that works
  - `Sentry.logger` log envelopes
  Known limits:
  - On Bun only libraries that publish `node:diagnostics_channel` events themselves are instrumented under a plain `bun app.ts`; every other instrumented library needs the plugin build above. The failure is silent: with `debug: true` the SDK logs "No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping" and still reports "Integration installed: Mysql", and without `debug` there is no output at all.
  - Every event, transaction and span reports `sdk.name: "sentry.javascript.bun"`, never `sentry.javascript.elysia`, under both init placements and both lifecycles.
  - Events captured inside a handler carry no transaction name, because the name is set after the handler runs.
  - The SDK's own hooks are visible in every trace as `sentryOnRequest`, `sentryOnAfterHandle` and `sentryOnError` spans, and the first pool use adds `db mysql2.pool.connect` and `db mysql2.connect`.

  **Change:** `guides/elysia/index.mdx`: add a "Database and library instrumentation on Bun" section after Configure with the bundle recipe and the "no `external`" rule. Leave the alert at `:47-50` as it is; the run confirms it. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:11`: qualify "No additional runtime instrumentation needed" for the database and library case. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:1`: drop the `BrowserTracing` paragraph from this server guide. `platform-includes/performance/what-instrumentation-provides/javascript.elysia.mdx:5`: the observed ops are `handler` and `middleware`, not `request_handler.elysia` and `middleware.elysia`. `platform-includes/performance/enable-stream-mode/javascript.elysia.mdx:25`: the `traceLifecycle` default is `'stream'`, not `'static'`. DOC-R1 covers javascript.bun.mdx, javascript.deno.mdx and javascript.cloudflare.mdx, not this file.
  Draft: [Add a Bun database instrumentation section to the Elysia guide and fix four include statements](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#54-add-a-bun-database-instrumentation-section-to-the-elysia-guide-and-fix-four-include-statements>)

title: Bun
body:
Docs changes for the Bun guide that a new user hits between install and the first event on v11, from the runtime docs audit (develop `03aaf42455` and `6f2da7483d`, docs `aebda0ee4`). Each item links to its issue draft in the secret gist (https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21); the reproductions are [`quickstarts/bun/`](<https://github.com/JPeer264/sentry-repros/tree/issue-linear-runtime-improvements/quickstarts/bun>) in the audit repository.

## Must land

- [ ] **P0** · DOC-B1 · The instrumentation step is backwards and never names the plugin
  The Bun guide at `guides/bun/index.mdx:88` and `:100` tells the user to run `bun --preload ./instrument.js app.js`, and the alert at `:90-94` states that Sentry's auto-instrumentation does not work with bundled code and that bundling requires manual instrumentation. `@sentry/bun/plugin` is not named anywhere on the page, and `logs` is used as an onboarding block at `:182` but is missing from the options at `:20-22`.
  What was observed on bun 1.4.0: a bundle built with `Bun.build({ plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` from `@sentry/bun/plugin` records library and framework spans, while running the same app unbundled with `bun run` records none. `packages/bun/src/plugin.ts:14` states the plugin is build-only. The unbundled diagnostic message is printed only with `debug: true`.
  **Change:** Keep the `--preload` step, described as what guarantees init order. Add a "Build with the Sentry plugin" step showing `Bun.build({ entrypoints: [...], plugins: [sentryBunPlugin()] })` imported from `@sentry/bun/plugin`. Replace the alert at `:90-94` with a plain statement: library and framework instrumentation requires a build with the plugin; `bun run` on unbundled source records manual spans plus `Bun.serve`, `node:http` and `fetch` spans. Add `logs` to the onboarding options at `:20-22`, or remove the block at `:182`.
  Draft: [Rewrite the Bun guide's instrumentation step around @sentry/bun/plugin](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#27-rewrite-the-bun-guides-instrumentation-step-around-sentrybunplugin>)

## Should land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-B2 · The integrations table does not match what the SDK installs
  `platform-includes/configuration/integrations/javascript.bun.mdx:5-37` lists `dedupeIntegration` (`:9`), `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` (`:24`) and `inboundFiltersIntegration` (`:14`) as auto-enabled, and `pinoIntegration` at `:47`, while `fsIntegration` is shown for Bun with no row.
  What was observed: the Bun SDK installs 42 integrations at `6f2da7483d`, and 43 on develop head, where `mastraIntegration()` joined `getTracingIntegrations()`. It ships `fetchIntegration` rather than `nativeNodeFetchIntegration`, installs inbound filtering as `EventFilters`, and does not install `dedupeIntegration`. Integrations installed with no row in the table: `fetchIntegration`, `bunHttpServerIntegration`, `processSessionIntegration`, `expressIntegration`, `fastifyIntegration`, `hapiIntegration`, `koaIntegration`, `awsIntegration`, `langGraphIntegration`, `postgresJsIntegration`, `spanStreamingIntegration` and `mastraIntegration`. The list is produced by `getDefaultIntegrations()` in `packages/bun/src/sdk.ts:77-79`, which spreads `getDefaultIntegrationsWithoutPerformance()` at `:47-74`, plus `packages/server-utils/src/integrations/index.ts:30-62` (`:30-63` on develop head). `spanStreamingIntegration` is not part of that list: the client adds it in `packages/core/src/server-runtime-client.ts:56`, so a table generated from `getDefaultIntegrations()` alone would still miss it. The channel-based integrations only produce spans after a `Bun.build` with `@sentry/bun/plugin`.
  **Change:** Drop the `dedupeIntegration` row; rename `nativeNodeFetchIntegration` to `fetchIntegration`; rename `inboundFiltersIntegration` to the installed `eventFiltersIntegration`. Add rows for the twelve installed integrations listed above. Add a "Requires `@sentry/bun/plugin`" column and tick it for the channel-based rows. Fix the gating so `common/configuration/integrations/pino.mdx` is shown for Bun, and give `fsIntegration` a row or hide it.
  Note: inboundFilters row overlaps SDK-1481.
  Draft: [Correct the Bun integrations table in platform-includes/.../javascript.bun.mdx](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#40-correct-the-bun-integrations-table-in-platform-includesjavascriptbunmdx>)
- [ ] **P2** · DOC-Q4 · Two warnings on the documented path that no page explains
  Following the "Apply Instrumentation to Your App" step at `guides/bun/index.mdx:82-105` as written, `bun --preload ./instrument.ts app.ts` (the command at `:100`) with `debug: true` prints `No available Node API to register diagnostics-channel injection hooks; skipping.` at startup and `[Sentry] No diagnostics-channel injection detected. Channel-based integrations will not record spans. Make sure the diagnostics channels are injected via the runtime --import hook or a bundler plugin before the instrumented modules load.` after the first request. Neither line is mentioned on the Bun guide or the troubleshooting pages, and the guide names no bundler plugin (DOC-B1).
  Observed on `develop` with bun 1.4.2: the warnings are correct. The first comes from `packages/server-runtime-injection/src/register.ts:160` (`:201` at develop head), the second from `packages/server-utils/src/orchestrion/detect.ts:38-42`; both go through `debug.warn`, so they print only with `debug: true`. Runtime instrumentation (`Bun.serve`, fetch, errors, logs) works on the documented path, and library instrumentation needs the `Bun.build` with `sentryBunPlugin()`. A reader who sees the warning has no page that says which of the two it refers to.
  **Change:** Quote both lines on the Bun guide next to the run command at `:100`, say that they print only with `debug: true` and that runtime instrumentation is unaffected, and link the plugin build step from DOC-B1 as the fix for library spans.
  Draft: [Explain the channel-injection warnings on the Bun guide](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#162-explain-the-channel-injection-warnings-on-the-bun-guide>)
- [ ] **P2** · DOC-B4 · No Bun version floor, npm install in the Hono tab, no breadcrumbs page
  `guides/bun/index.mdx:12` pulls the `getting-started-prerequisites` include, but no `javascript.bun.mdx` variant of it exists, so the page falls back to `_default.mdx` and states no Bun version floor. `guides/hono/index.mdx:84-85` installs the Bun SDK with `npm install @sentry/bun`, while the Bun guide uses `bun add`. `platform-includes/performance/automatic-instrumentation-intro/javascript.bun.mdx:1` still says the SDK "provides a `Tracing` integration", which is v7 wording.

## Must land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-D1 · No instrumentation step; the import hook is undocumented
  `guides/deno/index.mdx` renders `import * as Sentry from "npm:@sentry/deno"` through the `___SDK_PACKAGE___` placeholder at `:44` and `:66` (the literal specifier is not in the file), and shows two permission flags. It never states that the database, messaging, AI and framework integrations in the default set require the `@sentry/deno/import` hook, nor that the `Deno.serve` and `node:http` server spans work without it. `packages/deno/README.md:60-83` has a version of this section, but its `--import=@sentry/deno/import` form at `:70` does not resolve.
  What was observed on deno 2.9.0 and 2.8.3: a first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';` before `Sentry.init` registers the hook and instruments `mysql.createConnection`. `--import=@sentry/deno/import` fails with `Module not found`; `--import=./node_modules/@sentry/deno/build/import.mjs` registers the hook. Without the hook the SDK installs 39 integrations at `6f2da7483d`, reports no injection and prints nothing. The `deno-mysql` and `deno-pg` e2e apps use the first-line import form, with `nodeModulesDir: "manual"` and an installed `node_modules`. Any dependency that `require()`s a JSON file currently crashes under the hook.
  **Change:** Add an "Enable library instrumentation" step to `guides/deno/index.mdx` with first-line `import '@sentry/deno/import';` as the primary form. State that the hook needs the package resolvable from `node_modules`, so `deno.json` has to set `nodeModulesDir` to `"auto"`, or to `"manual"` with an install step, which is what every Deno e2e app does. Show the file-path `--import` flag as the alternative; do not show the bare specifier form. State that dependencies which `require()` a JSON file fail to import under the hook. State which instrumentation works without the hook.
  Draft: [Document the @sentry/deno/import hook in the Deno guide](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#42-document-the-sentrydenoimport-hook-in-the-deno-guide>)
- [ ] **P1** · DOC-D3 · The documented permission flags crash the app under the hook, and silently degrade without it
  `guides/deno/index.mdx:100` shows `deno run --allow-net=<ingest> index.ts` and `:119` shows `deno run --allow-read=./src index.ts` as two separate commands, while the init snippets on the same page name the file `main.ts`. Neither `--allow-env` nor `--allow-sys` is mentioned, and `packages/deno/README.md` mentions no flag at all.
  What was observed on deno 2.9.0: with only `--allow-net` and `--no-prompt`, events carry `server_name: null`, no OS version, an absolute filesystem path as the frame filename and no context lines. With the `@sentry/deno/import` hook line present, the same flags do not degrade but crash: `NotCapable: Requires env access, run again with the --allow-env flag`, raised from the vendored `debug` package inside `@sentry/server-runtime-injection` at module load (getting-started reproduction QS-deno, 2026-09-08). With all permissions granted, the same app reports the hostname, the OS version, an `app:///`-prefixed filename and context lines. No warning is printed in the restricted run. Every Deno e2e app runs with `--allow-net --allow-env --allow-read`; `deno-mysql`, `deno-pg` and `deno-redis` add `--allow-sys --allow-write`, and `deno-streamed` adds `--allow-sys`.
  **Change:** Replace the two commands at `:100` and `:119` with a single `deno run --allow-net=<ingest> --allow-read --allow-env --allow-sys main.ts`, using the same filename as the init snippets. Add a table naming what each flag unlocks: `--allow-net` event delivery, `--allow-read` source context lines and app-relative frame paths, `--allow-env` `SENTRY_*` lookups and `serverName`, `--allow-sys` hostname and OS version. Add the same table to `packages/deno/README.md`.
  Draft: [Show one complete deno run command with all four permission flags in the Deno guide](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#44-show-one-complete-deno-run-command-with-all-four-permission-flags-in-the-deno-guide>)
- [ ] **P0** · DOC-R2 · The crons page recommends an integration that crashes init on Deno 2.9
  `platform-includes/crons/setup/javascript.deno.mdx:1` heads its first section "Automatic Check-Ins (Recommended)" and `:12` tells the reader to pass `Sentry.denoCronIntegration()` to `Sentry.init`.
  That call crashes startup on Deno 2.9.0 and later. `packages/deno/src/integrations/deno-cron.ts:23` assigns `Deno.cron = new Proxy(Deno.cron, ...)` inside `setupOnce`, i.e. inside `Sentry.init`. On Deno 2.8.3 `Deno.cron` is a writable data property and the integration works: a cron firing at the minute boundary produced one `in_progress` and one `ok` check-in. From Deno 2.9.0 `Deno.cron` is a getter-only accessor, so the assignment throws `TypeError: Cannot set property cron of #<Object> which has only a getter` and the process exits 1 before any user code runs.
  There is a second failure mode without the unstable flag. When `Deno.cron` is absent the guard at `deno-cron.ts:18-21` returns silently, so the integration is an inert no-op and the SDK gives no warning, while the reader's own `Deno.cron(...)` call throws `TypeError: Deno.cron is not a function`. The integration is also not in the Deno default set (`packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:31-49`), although its own JSDoc at `deno-cron.ts:64` says "Enabled by default in the Deno SDK".
  **Change:** Remove the "Recommended" framing and the `denoCronIntegration()` snippet, or state that it makes `Sentry.init` throw on Deno 2.9.0 and later and works only up to Deno 2.8.3. Lead with the `Sentry.withMonitor` / `Sentry.captureCheckIn` sections already on the page. State that `Deno.cron` needs `--unstable-cron`, and that without the flag the integration silently does nothing. Say that the integration has to be passed in `integrations` explicitly; it is not in the Deno default set.
  Draft: [Stop recommending denoCronIntegration() on the Deno crons page](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#29-stop-recommending-denocronintegration-on-the-deno-crons-page>)

Outgoing `fetch` produces breadcrumbs only. The library integrations need the `@sentry/deno/import` hook. The installed list comes from `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:28-49`.
  **Change:** Rewrite the table from `packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:28-49` so every installed integration has a row. Add a "Requires `@sentry/deno/import`" column and tick the library, messaging and AI rows. Add rows for `denoServeIntegration` and `denoHttpIntegration`, noting they produce Deno transactions, and state that outgoing `fetch` yields breadcrumbs only. Fix the cell count of row `:21`. Remove `javascript.deno` from the `supported:` list of the `modules`, `onuncaughtexception`, `unhandledrejection` and `console` common pages. Remove `javascript.deno` from the `notSupported` list of `common/configuration/integrations/breadcrumbs.mdx`: the Deno SDK installs `breadcrumbsIntegration()` (`packages/deno/src/sdk.ts:39`) and exports it (`packages/deno/src/index.ts:164`).

- [ ] **P2** · DOC-D6 · Install shows only the npm: specifier; deno add and the import map are missing
  `guides/deno/index.mdx:38-46` says to "Import the Sentry Deno SDK directly from the npm registry", and every snippet on the page renders `npm:@sentry/deno` from the `___SDK_PACKAGE___` placeholder (the literal specifier is not in the file). `guides/hono/index.mdx:88-89` is the only page showing `deno add npm:@sentry/deno`. While in `enable-stream-mode/javascript.deno.mdx`, note that `:24` calls `traceLifecycle: 'static'` "the default", which holds for the released line only; DOC-Q1 tracks that sentence across all ten runtime variants of the include.

There is no error-capture path on that plumbing, on either trace lifecycle.
  The fix belongs in the app, so the page can show it: `ctx.waitUntil(work().catch((e) => Sentry.captureException(e)));`.
  **Change:** Add a sentence stating that errors thrown or rejected inside `ctx.waitUntil()` are not captured, on either trace lifecycle. Show the app-side fix, `ctx.waitUntil(work().catch((e) => Sentry.captureException(e)));`, next to the existing sample. Retitle the section so it does not read as complete `waitUntil` coverage. Confirmed for Pages on 2026-09-09: `context.waitUntil(Promise.reject(new Error(...)))` in a Pages function was not captured, workerd logged `Uncaught Error` and only the request segment arrived; the section shows Worker code only (QS-cloudflare-pages, variant base).

  Several Cloudflare includes show code that does not match the package or the guide's own contract. `platform-includes/tracing/traces-sampler/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:4` calls `Sentry.browserTracingIntegration()`. `platform-includes/tracing/sample-rate/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:1-7` and the `capture-console` (`:1-8`) and `dedupe` (`:1-8`) configuration includes show a bare `Sentry.init(...)`. `platform-includes/configuration/contextlines/javascript.cloudflare.mdx` exists but `contextlines.mdx` lists `cloudflare` under `notSupported`, so it never renders. `guides/cloudflare/index.mdx:38-40` and `:356-360` contain a `logs` onboarding block that is not in the button list. `frameworks/nextjs.mdx:40` and `getting-started-config/javascript.cloudflare.mdx:5` state compatibility dates of 2025-08-16 and 2024-09-23 without saying which applies to whom. `frameworks/hydrogen-remix.mdx:59` contains a literal `YOUR_DSN_HERE`.

Remove `cloudflare` from `notSupported` in `contextlines.mdx` or delete the unreachable Cloudflare include, leaving the Bun and Deno includes in place. Add `logs` to the onboarding buttons.   `platform-includes/getting-started-verify/javascript.mdx:53-68` tells the reader to update the button handler so that it starts a span around a simulated longer operation, and shows `function triggerError() { await Sentry.startSpan(...) }`. The function is not `async`.

With `async function triggerError()` the same page produces the span (`test Example Frontend Span`) inside the pageload span envelope.

## Should land

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q8 · The CDN tab names the tracing bundle and adds replayIntegration(), which records nothing
  `platform-includes/getting-started-config/javascript.mdx:116` names `bundle.tracing.min.js` in the CDN tab, and the same snippet adds `Sentry.replayIntegration()` at `:130` and `:133`.
  Observed with that combination on the develop CDN build: the console shows `warning: You are using replayIntegration() even though this bundle does not include replay.`, `Replay` still appears in the installed integrations, no event carries a `replayId` tag, and no replay envelope is ever sent. With `bundle.tracing.replay.min.js` the same page records the replay.
  **Change:** Name `bundle.tracing.replay.min.js` in the CDN tab, or remove `replayIntegration()` and the replay sample rates from the CDN variant of the snippet. State that a bundle without replay turns `replayIntegration()` into a no-op with a console warning only.

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q9 · Sentry.logger is a silent no-op on the CDN bundles and no page says which bundle has logs
  The logs quick start (`includes/logs/javascript-quick-start-verify-logs-splitlayout.mdx:13`) tells every browser reader to call `Sentry.logger.info(...)`; the CDN install tab of the browser guide names `bundle.tracing.min.js`. Neither says that the CDN bundles ship a stub logger.
  Observed on develop: with the npm package and the CommonJS build the log item arrives. With `bundle.tracing.min.js` and with `bundle.tracing.replay.min.js` no log envelope is produced and nothing warns; in the bundle `Sentry.logger` and `Sentry.metrics` are objects whose methods are empty functions. The v10-to-v11 page mentions the metrics half only (`common/migration/v10-to-v11/index.mdx:1398`).
  **Change:** On the logs pages that render for the browser, say that `Sentry.logger` is a no-op on the CDN bundles that do not include logs, and name the bundle that does. Add the same sentence next to the CDN tab of the browser config page.

- [ ] **P1** · DOC-Q63 · Debug IDs need a build_id section and a streaming loader the guide never mentions
  `guides/wasm/index.mdx:65` says the integration provides Debug IDs, Debug Files, Code IDs, Code Files and memory addresses. With a module that has no `build_id` custom section (nothing in the guide's install or Rust steps adds one; `wasm-split` does) the event carries only `instruction_addr` and `platform: native` on the wasm frame, no `addr_mode` and no `debug_meta`: the registry skips modules without `build_id`. The page never mentions `wasm-split`, `build_id`, DWARF or the debug file upload.
  Loading also matters and the page (`:160`, `:176-179`) is silent on it: a module loaded with `WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes)` after `fetch().arrayBuffer()` is named `wasm://wasm/<hash>` by Chrome, so even with `build_id` no image matches and no `addr_mode` or `debug_meta` is attached; `instantiateStreaming` and `compileStreaming` keep the URL and match.
  **Change:** State at `:65` that the module must carry a `build_id` section (`wasm-split`) and that the DWARF debug file has to be uploaded, link the debug files docs, and add that symbolication needs a loader that keeps the module URL.
  Draft: [Say on the WebAssembly guide what the integration needs: a build_id section, a URL-keeping loader and uploaded debug files](<https://gist.github.com/JPeer264/6d973a8266700d0cecbca9ed27cf8b21#130-say-on-the-webassembly-guide-what-the-integration-needs-a-build_id-section-a-url-keeping-loader-and-uploaded-debug-files>)
